bull.b: Sustained, sizable operating and free cash flow provides durable funding for R&D, product rollout, M&A and opportunistic buybacks without relying on equity raises. This cash profile materially reduces financing risk and supports multi‑year execution despite GAAP losses.

SaaS‑style gross margins and recent non‑GAAP margin expansion reflect strong unit economics and operating leverage. Durable margin advantage supports profit conversion as revenue scales and provides buffer versus cost pressures like AI compute over the next 2–3 years.

Accretive M&A and rapid product adoption strengthen competitive moat: reality capture + AI deepens data advantage, improves automation on job sites, expands TAM and cross‑sell opportunities, and helps address chronic construction labor/productivity gaps over the medium term.

bear.b: Accounting profitability remains elusive at the operating line, meaning reported earnings may lag cash profitability. Persistent GAAP losses limit return metrics, may constrain certain institutional demand, and create execution risk if higher investments fail to convert to sustained GAAP profit.

A durable slowdown in headline revenue growth reduces operating‑leverage uplift and raises the bar for margin expansion to offset slower top‑line gains. Contract duration effects and normalization of CRPO suggest some backlog strength may fade across the next 2–4 quarters.

Large convertible issuance, capped calls and planned bridge financing introduce dilution and covenant/structure complexity. This can constrain future capital flexibility, increase oversight triggers and create execution risk if M&A synergies or integration take longer than planned.
